claims.claim: Faulty inverter AC available for sale.
claims.evidence: Witness photos show a white portable air conditioner, but do not show inverter branding, and do not show any test result proving it is faulty.

risks.risk: Whether it actually works (cooling/heating performance, compressor operation, airflow).
risks.proof: Short video/clip of the unit powered on showing temperature change and steady airflow (and any error code on the display, if present).

risks.risk: Inverter claim may be wrong (could be non-inverter), affecting value and parts compatibility.
risks.proof: Clear close-up photo of the front label/model plate showing inverter/non-inverter designation and exact model.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a generic portable AC without inverter premium.

risks.risk: Missing accessories/parts (remote, drain hose, window kit/brackets) which can make it unusable or reduce usability.
risks.proof: Photo spread showing all included items laid out (remote, drain hose, window kit/brackets, manual) and a check of ports/slots on the unit.

risks.risk: Electrical condition (plug/cable wear, fuse/board health) and safety.
risks.proof: Photo of the plug and cable condition plus a clip of power-on without sparking/overheating and with stable operation.

risks.risk: Refrigerant/leak or need for recharge (common failure that may still power on but won’t cool).
risks.proof: Cooling test clip showing sustained cold air after several minutes; ideally include any service sticker/pressure test record if available.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as potentially needing refrigerant service.

risks.risk: Dirty/blocked filter or evaporator (reduces cooling and may indicate poor maintenance).
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the filter and evaporator area (with filter removed) showing cleanliness/mold/dust.

proof_requests: Send a clear close-up of the brand/model plate (including BTU/capacity and inverter/non-inverter wording).
Provide a short video of the unit powered on with the display visible, then show airflow and temperature drop over time.
Show all included accessories laid out (remote, drain hose, window kit/brackets) and confirm what is missing.
Upload photos of the plug/cable and any visible electrical damage.
Show the filter/evaporator condition (filter removed) in close-up.
response.reason: The witness confirms the item is a portable air conditioner, but key details (brand/model, capacity, and whether it is truly faulty/inverter) are not verifiable from the report. So it can be priced at the worst case for a portable AC with unknown working status and missing accessories.
